how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py (the repo's reader) run through a three-line wrapper that asks the render call by page name instead of by revision id, because www.mariowiki.com answers HTTP 403 to action=parse with an oldid; the licence line, revision lookup, text extraction and manifest are the reader's own code. Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word (white space collapsed) in the page text saved in build/wiki-live/mariowiki at the revision named. Table rows are quoted with their cells joined by ' || '. Several Super Mario Wiki pages describe the whole series; a line states a Mario Party 2 fact only where the page says so for Mario Party 2.

lines.line: Summary: An item that lets you roll two Dice Blocks instead of one and move the total of both. It costs 10 coins at an Item Shop and is Mario's favorite item; each character has one, and computer players go for theirs when they can.

quoted: When used, the Mushroom allows a player to roll two Dice Blocks instead of just one, traveling a number of spaces equal to the sum of the numbers rolled.
It can be bought from an Item Shop for 10 coins.
The Mushroom is Mario's favorite item in this game.
Each character has a "preferred" or "favorite" item
Whenever a computer player has the opportunity to get an item, they will go for their preferred item if possible.

lines.line: Uses: Use it on your turn to roll two Dice Blocks and move the sum of the two numbers. Rolling the same number on both gives you 10 coins, and double 7s give you 20 coins.

quoted: When used, this item allows the player to roll two Dice Blocks instead of one. The two digits that the player rolls are added up together, and the player will move that many spaces.
If the player rolls the same number on both Dice Blocks, they are granted 10 coins, or 20 coins for double 7s.

lines.line: Tips: At 10 coins it ties with the Skeleton Key as the cheapest item in the shop. You can carry only one item at a time, and with one in hand you cannot enter an Item Shop or start an Item Mini-Game, so use it before your next shop or Item Space.

quoted: All items sold at the Item Shop cost at least 10 coins
Mushroom || 10 coins || Skeleton Key || 10 coins || Plunder Chest || 15 coins
if they are already carrying an item, they will not be allowed to enter the shop
A player can only hold one item at a time in this game.
The Mini-Game will not be initiated if it is the last turn, or if the player already has an item.

lines.line: Summary: An item that lets you roll three Dice Blocks and move the total of all three. It costs 20 coins at an Item Shop.

quoted: When used, the player using it will roll three Dice Blocks. The digits of all three rolls are added together, and the player will move that many spaces.
Golden Mushroom || 20 coins

lines.line: Uses: Use it to roll three Dice Blocks and move the sum of the three numbers. If all three show the same number you get 20 coins, and three 7s give you 50 coins.

quoted: If the player rolls the same digits on all three Dice Blocks (e.g. three "10's"), the player gets 20 Coins. Three "7's" result in 50 Coins.

lines.line: Tips: It is on the shop's stock lists in the first five turns for some placings, and on every placing's list from the middle of the game on. On Bowser Land, walking past the Baby Bowser shop in a Bowser Suit makes him hand you one of four items for free: a Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom, Boo Bell or Magic Lamp.

quoted: Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom, Magic Lamp
If the player passes by this shop while wearing a Bowser Suit, he will instead give the player a Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom, Boo Bell, or a Magic Lamp for free.

lines.line: Summary: An item that opens a locked gate on a board when you reach it, usually giving access to areas you could not otherwise reach. It costs 10 coins at an Item Shop and is Luigi's favorite item.

quoted: that can unlock certain doors on a board, usually opening access to areas that cannot be reached otherwise.
The Skeleton Key can always be bought at Item Shops for 10 Coins in Mario Party 2
It is Luigi's favorite item in Mario Party 2 and 3
This item is activated automatically whenever a player who possesses it is about to run into a locked gate.
Skeleton Key || 10 coins

lines.line: Uses: At a locked gate the key opens it, you are let through, and the gate locks again. Using one only opens the door, so you can spend it on a door without actually taking that path.

quoted: The key will open the gate – the player will be let through, and the gate will be locked again.
Using one will only open the door, allowing the player to choose to spend it to open a door but not actually travel that path.

lines.line: Tips: You cannot throw it away to make room for another item: it stays until you use it on a door, unless another player steals it. Item Shops sell it for 10 coins everywhere except Bowser Land, where Baby Bowser can force one on you for 12.

quoted: Unlike in Mario Party 3, the player cannot discard this item if they do not need it.
Once acquired, a Skeleton Key cannot be discarded to make room for another item - it must be used on a door to get rid of it, if not stolen by another player.
The Skeleton Key can always be bought at Item Shops for 10 Coins in Mario Party 2, except in Bowser Land, unless Baby Bowser forces the player to buy one for 12 Coins.

lines.line: Summary: An item that steals an item from an opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Peach's favorite item.

quoted: It is a treasure chest that can steal an item from another player.
In Mario Party 2 and Mario Party 3, it is Princess Peach's favorite item
Plunder Chest || 15 coins

lines.line: Uses: Using it steals an item from an opponent picked at random out of all the opponents who are holding one; you cannot choose whom to rob. You can use the stolen item at once, unless it is a Bowser Bomb, or keep it for a later turn.

quoted: In Mario Party 2, when used, the Plunder Chest steals an item from another player, chosen at random out of all opponents that have items.
However, you cannot choose which opponent to steal.
The stolen item can then be used immediately (unless it is a Bowser Bomb), or held for a later turn as usual.

lines.line: Tips: In the Item Shop it shows up for the player in second place in the middle of the game and for the player in first place in the last five turns.

quoted: Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Golden Mushroom
Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom
!! Mid-game || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom
!! Last 5 turns || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom

lines.line: Summary: An item that lets you pick an opponent to duel in a Duel Mini-Game for coins. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Wario's favorite item.

quoted: The Dueling Glove is used to wager a number of coins decided by the user in Mario Party 2, as the two players compete in a duel minigame specific to the board.
It is Wario's favorite item
The Dueling Glove costs 15 coins to buy.

lines.line: Uses: Using it summons a Goomba, then you choose the opponent to duel and how many coins to wager. The most you can wager is the coin count of whichever of the two players has fewer coins before the duel.

quoted: When used, the player using it will summon a Goomba. The player will then choose an opponent to duel in a Duel Mini-Game. After this, the player will have the option to choose how much is to be dueled for.
The maximum amount of Coins the player can choose is equivalent to the amount of Coins of the participant who has the least amount of Coins prior to the duel.

lines.line: Tips: The wager is always coins. In the Item Shop it appears in the middle of the game for third and fourth place and in the last five turns for first and second place.

quoted: This is always Coins.
!! Mid-game || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom
!! Last 5 turns || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom

lines.line: Summary: An item that swaps your place on the board with a random opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Yoshi's favorite item.

quoted: It is a block that transports the user to another player's space and then swaps that player over to where the user was.
The Warp Block costs 15 Coins to buy at an Item Shop in Mario Party 2
The Warp Block is Yoshi's favorite item

lines.line: Uses: A Warp Block appears above you when you use it, and hitting it warps you and swaps positions with a randomly chosen opponent. You can still roll the regular Dice Block on the same turn.

quoted: When used, the Warp Block will appear above the player using it. The player will then hit the block – this causes the player to warp and exchange positions on the board with a randomly chosen opponent.
Unlike before, the player can use the regular Dice Block on the same turn.

lines.line: Tips: You can also win one from an Item Mini-Game. In the Item Shop it only shows up in the last five turns, for the players in second, third and fourth place, and on Bowser Land the forced sale costs 17 coins.

quoted: It can also be obtained during an Item mini-game.
at the secondary Item Shop in Bowser Land, it costs 17 coins.

!! Last 5 turns || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom, Magic Lamp
!! Mid-game || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom

lines.line: Summary: An item that takes you straight to the Star Space. At 30 coins it is the most expensive item in the Item Shop.

quoted: When used, the player summons the Mushroom Genie. He gives the player a ride on his back and takes the player directly to the Star Space.
Magic Lamp || 30 coins
Mushroom || 10 coins || Skeleton Key || 10 coins || Plunder Chest || 15 coins || Dueling Glove || 15 coins || Warp Block || 15 coins || Golden Mushroom || 20 coins || Magic Lamp || 30 coins

lines.line: Uses: Using it summons the Mushroom Genie, who gives you a ride to the Star Space, where you are asked whether you want to trade 20 coins for a Star.

quoted: The player is then asked whether they wish to trade 20 Coins for a Star or not.
The Mushroom Genie appears and takes you straight to Toad.

lines.line: Tips: You still pay 20 coins for the Star when you arrive, on top of the 30 it costs to buy. The shop offers it only in the last five turns, to third and fourth place. When Bowser's Multiplying Toads puts two Toads on the board, a Magic Lamp always takes you to the real one.

quoted: The player is then asked whether they wish to trade 20 Coins for a Star or not.

!! Last 5 turns || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Plunder Chest, Dueling Glove, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Dueling Glove, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom || Mushroom, Skeleton Key, Warp Block, Golden Mushroom, Magic Lamp
In the Bowser's Multiplying Toads event of Mario Party 2
a Genie Lamp always takes the user to the real Toad

lines.line: Summary: An item that calls a Boo to steal coins or a Star from an opponent. In this game it comes only from Item Mini-Games, and neither kind of Item Shop sells it.

quoted: Its use is to ring for Boo and ask him to steal coins or a star
The Boo Bell first appears in Mario Party 2, where it can be obtained in an Item Minigame only.
Neither type of Item Shop sells Boo Bells.

lines.line: Uses: Using it summons a Boo, who asks whom to steal from. Stealing coins costs you five coins and stealing a Star costs 50 coins, and the Boo can take at most 30 coins or one Star.

quoted: When used, the player using it will summon a Boo. Boo will then ask the player whom to steal from, whether it be Coins (this costs five Coins), or a Star (this costs 50 Coins).
Additionally, the Boo can only steal a maximum of 30 coins or a maximum of one Star.

lines.line: Tips: If a Boo is stealing coins from you, press the A button quickly to fight it off. Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can also give you a Boo Bell for free, as one of four possible gifts, if you pass it in a Bowser Suit.

quoted: If the Boo tries to steal Coins, the opponent can fight it off by pressing the A button quickly.
If the player passes by this shop while wearing a Bowser Suit, he will instead give the player a Skeleton Key, Golden Mushroom, Boo Bell, or a Magic Lamp for free.

lines.line: Summary: A rare item that disguises you as Bowser and lets you steal 20 coins from any opponent you pass. You usually win it in an Item Mini-Game.

quoted: The Bowser Suit makes its debut in Mario Party 2 as a rare item resembling Bowser's face, obtainable only during Item Minigames.
When used, the player using it will masquerade themselves as Bowser and steals 20 Coins from any opponent they pass.

lines.line: Uses: When used you put on a full-body suit in the likeness of Bowser's body, and you steal 20 coins from any opponent you pass.

quoted: When used, the user dons a full-body suit in the likeness of Bowser's body and can steal 20 Coins from players they pass
steals 20 Coins from any opponent they pass.

lines.line: Tips: Wearing it changes how Baby Bowsers deal with you: the one on the board always gives you coins when you pass, and on Bowser Land you can change the parade's route for free unless it is the last move, collect 20 coins at the Bowser Bank and get a free item from the forced shop. The regular Item Shops do not sell the suit, but Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can force one on you for 12 coins.

quoted: He will always give the player coins if they are using a Bowser Suit.

If the player uses a Bowser Suit and passes by the Bowser Parade Planning Office, the Baby Bowser mistakes the player for Bowser and allows them to change the route of the parade for free unless it is the last move.
Passing the Bowser Bank in the suit also grants the player 20 Coins.
passing the shop ran by the Baby Bowser Shopkeeper grants the player with a Skeleton Key, a Golden Mushroom, a Boo Bell, or a Magic Lamp for free.
Bowser Suits and Bowser Bombs are not sold at Koopa Troopa's shops, but they may be sold by Baby Bowser's shop.
Bowser Suit || 12 coins

lines.line: Summary: A rare item that is not yours to aim: if you get one, Bowser uses it at the end of the current turn, and anyone he passes loses all their coins. It is Donkey Kong's favorite item.

quoted: When a player obtains this item in an Item Mini-Game, Bowser will use it at the end of the current turn.
Any player that Bowser passes will lose all of their Coins.
This is Donkey Kong's favorite item.

lines.line: Uses: At the end of the turn Baby Bowser turns into Bowser, rolls three Dice Blocks and moves around the board that many spaces, taking all the coins from every player he passes.

quoted: When used, Baby Bowser will transform into Bowser. Bowser will then roll three Dice Blocks, and will move accordingly.
who will hit three Dice Blocks and then travel around the board, stealing all coins from any player he passes.

lines.line: Tips: Besides Item Mini-Games, the only way to get one is Baby Bowser's forced sale on Bowser Land, at 12 coins. If you steal one with a Plunder Chest you cannot use it right away. If it goes off while Bowser's Multiplying Toads has put two Toads on the board, it shows which Toad is the false one.

quoted: or even a Bowser Bomb (the only way to obtain one outside of item minigames), each costing 12 Coins
The stolen item can then be used immediately (unless it is a Bowser Bomb), or held for a later turn as usual.
If a Bowser Bomb is used, it will expose the fake Toad as a Baby Bowser.

lines.line: Summary: A henchman of Bowser's who stands on every board beside Toad and steals 5 coins from any player who passes him. Now and then he gives you 5 coins instead and later says it was an accident.

quoted: A single Baby Bowser appears on every board in the game, in a similar capacity to Toad, who sells Stars.
If a player passes Baby Bowser, he will steal 5 Coins from that player. However, he occasionally gives a player 5 Coins instead, later claiming that this was an accident.
This is a henchman of Bowser's. He will steal five coins from you when you pass in front of him.

lines.line: Weak points: He always gives you coins instead of taking them if you are wearing a Bowser Suit. He starts at one of several set spots beside Toad and moves to Toad's old spot each time the Star is bought.

quoted: He will always give the player coins if they are using a Bowser Suit.
He is initially placed in one of several predetermined locations on the board alongside Toad, and every time that the Star is bought from Toad, he will move to Toad's previous location.

lines.line: Looks like: A miniature version of Bowser.

quoted: The Koopa Kids resemble miniature versions of Bowser
and formerly known as Baby Bowsers prior to Mario Party 4

lines.line: Tips: Expect to lose 5 coins each time you pass him, since the gift is only occasional. A Bowser Bomb briefly swaps him for Bowser at the end of the turn, and so does a Bowser Space roulette result called Bowser's Appearing Act.

quoted: If a player passes Baby Bowser, he will steal 5 Coins from that player. However, he occasionally gives a player 5 Coins instead
Baby Bowser will briefly be replaced by Bowser at the end of the turn
This also occurs if someone lands on a Bowser Space and the roulette lands on Bowser's Appearing Act.

lines.line: Summary: A parade led by Baby Bowser that travels a set path across Bowser Land and sends anyone it catches back to the start.

quoted: The Bowser Parade is a parade that occurs regularly in Bowser Land from Mario Party 2. It is led by Baby Bowser
The Bowser Parade travels down a set path
Anyone caught in the parade's path will be sent back to the start

lines.line: Weak points: If nobody is in its path once it starts, Baby Bowser cancels it. At the parade offices at the north, west and east intersections you can pay Baby Bowser five coins to change its direction, and in a Bowser Suit that is free unless it is the last move.

quoted: If nobody appears to be in the Bowser Parade's path once the parade starts, Baby Bowser will cancel it.
there are special parade offices at the intersections at the north, west, and east ends of the board, where players can pay Baby Bowser five coins to change the direction of the parade if they wish.
allows them to change the route of the parade for free unless it is the last move.

lines.line: Looks like: Pyramid-shaped floats that look like enemies such as Goomba, Boo and Thwomp, led by Baby Bowser.

quoted: It is led by Baby Bowser, and consists of several pyramid-shaped floats, which resemble enemies such as Goomba, Boo, and Thwomp.

lines.line: Tips: It always starts at the central intersection at the north end of the board, and its initial path runs straight to the south end and then east toward the starting area.

quoted: which always starts at the central intersection at the north end of Bowser Land.
The Bowser Parade's initial path just travels straight to the south end of the board, and then east towards the starting area.

lines.line: Summary: A giant Boo on Horror Land who, like a normal Boo, steals coins or Stars, but from every opponent at once.

quoted: In Mario Party 2, Big Boo appears in the Horror Land stage.
As with a typical Boo, it is able to steal objects from player's rivals, being coins or stars.
Unlike normal Boos, he will steal from all players at once.

lines.line: Weak points: You can only ask for him at night.

quoted: Characters can ask for him only in night time

lines.line: Looks like: In the daytime he appears as a giant Boo statue.

quoted: in daytime, Big Boo appears as a giant Boo statue.

lines.line: Tips: Because the night-time path to him needs a Skeleton Key, meeting him is difficult and rare.

quoted: Since Big Boo can only be visited at night after taking a path that requires the Skeleton Key, meeting him proves to be a difficult and rare opportunity for players

lines.line: Summary: A space that summons Bowser, and an event picked from the Bowser Roulette then plays out: a bad or game-changing event for the player who landed there, and sometimes for the other players too.

quoted: When a player lands on this space, Bowser will be summoned. An event chosen from the Bowser Roulette will then unfold.
they cause Bowser to appear and cause a major negative or otherwise game-altering event for the player who landed on the space, but this event can directly affect other players as well.

lines.line: Weak points: If you have no coins when you land on a Coins for Bowser result, Bowser gives you 10 coins instead. The 10,000 Coin Present, 100 Star Present, Star Steal and Stars-Packed to Go results can come up on the roulette, but Bowser then leaves without doing anything.

quoted: If the player does not have any Coins when landing on this event, Bowser will give them 10 Coins.
While the roulette is capable of landing on these events unlike in the first game, Bowser will leave without doing anything if it happens.

lines.line: Tips: Coins for Bowser is the most common result and appears twice on the wheel, and Bowser's Coin Potluck takes coins from all four players: 10 coins in the first five turns, 30 in the last five and 20 otherwise. Bowser's Multiplying Toads puts two Toads on the board, moves the Star Space and adds a second one; paying the false Toad 20 coins gets you a Ztar that does not count as a Star, a Magic Lamp always leads to the real Toad, and a Bowser Bomb exposes the false one.

quoted: It has become the most common event, always appearing twice on the roulette wheel.
Bowser's Coin Potluck: This is similar to Coins for Bowser, but Bowser takes Coins from all four players.
10 Coins if in the first five turns
30 Coins if in the last five turns
20 Coins otherwise
Bowser does a "magic" trick that makes two Toads appear on the board. This moves the Star Space's position, adding a second Star Space as well.
Anyone who pays him 20 Coins for a Star makes him reveal himself and give them a Ztar (which does not affect the player's Star count). A Magic Lamp always leads the player to the real Toad.
If a Bowser Bomb is used, it will expose the fake Toad as a Baby Bowser.
